name: GPU Fluid Overlay
summary: A realtime GPU fluid simulation runs OVER photographic plates or a dark stage: the cursor injects dye and momentum, so smoke-like neon vapor swirls, lingers, and dissipates in the visitor's wake. The visitor co-authors the hero in real time while a pinned monumental headline anchors the frame.

composition: One monumental anchored word is the only fixed typographic mass; the fluid needs a still element to swirl against or the frame reads as chaos.
The fluid field is full-bleed — cropping it into a panel kills the immersion.
A thin scene-selector rail can swap preset dye palettes/imagery, proving the effect is an engine, not a one-off.
layering: The vapor deliberately crosses BOTH in front of and behind the headline letters, fusing the sim and type into one volume.
A subject cutout or photo can be woven into the vapor midground — fluid over photography, the effects-layered method from the PLAN diagnosis.
UI chrome stays on the frontmost plane, minimal and stable.
lighting: The fluid IS the light source: emissive self-lit dye on a near-black vignetted stage, additive-style hot cores where trails overlap, soft falloff at edges.
Everything else in frame is graded around the dye color so the vapor is the brightest, most saturated element.
typography: Heavy condensed uppercase display, one word, static — the fluid animates around it so it feels kinetic without moving.
Tiny mono/label UI at the edges; nothing mid-scale.

rules: Near-black base + ONE emissive dye family per scene; the palette swaps with the scene preset rather than mixing hues in one frame.
The dye color doubles as brand accent — CTA and highlights borrow it.

easing: No keyframed easing — the sim's own physics (velocity advection, diffusion, decay) IS the ease; damping constants are the design surface.
Dissipation should linger ~1-2s after input stops: the wake is the delight.
pacing: Continuous low-level ambient turbulence at idle; spikes on cursor input then settles.
Scene swaps are quick (~1s crossfade) so the engine's range shows without dead time.
choreography: Cursor leads, fluid follows and lingers — a lead/echo relationship between user motion and pigment.
Fast sweeps tear big vortices; slow drifts swell gently — input velocity maps to visual energy.

gapNotes: The physics/fluid pack ships 36 TSL sim primitives, but a cursor-driven dye-injection Navier-Stokes field composited OVER photographic plates has not been demonstrated as a hub background — needs a pointer-force + dye-source binding into the hub background layer.
Type-volume fusion (vapor passing in front of AND behind letters) needs depth-sorted compositing between the sim layer and text meshes — unproven.
Bloom post-pass exists in the marketing stack but is not part of the R1 cinematic floor in the prism runtime (W-PHOTO).

whenToUse: Tech/creative/AI products that must demonstrate GPU craft in the first second.
Dark-stage heroes where a single brand hue should own the frame.
Surfaces where visitor interaction is the message — the effect proves responsiveness.
whenNotToUse: Text-heavy or accessibility-first pages — constant turbulence fights readability and must fully respect reduced-motion.
Low-power/mobile GPUs: per-frame sim is a battery/jank risk; needs a static-gradient fallback.
Calm, editorial, or trust-first registers (finance, health) — reads as spectacle.

notes: One full-frame GPU effect per surface — fluid, particles, and glitch compete for the same motion budget and GPU frame time.
The pinned headline is not optional: every observed instance anchors the turbulence with one still monumental word.

antiRepetition.notes: Same cluster as particle-field-hero and hover-morph-distortion — all full-frame pointer-reactive GPU fields.

sources.motionEvidence: Founder live analysis recorded in PRISM-DESIGN-SUPREMACY-PLAN.md §1 (realtime GPU fluid shaders OVER photographic plates/cutouts), corroborated by the monitor session's live demo: cursor sweeps at varied velocity injected dye that swirled and decayed; scene-selector rail exercised across presets (neon cyber, chromatic vapor, botanical, spice).

exemplars.promptSummary: Viscous oily ink folding across a dark field with thin-film soap-bubble iridescence through magenta/teal/gold — the iridescent fluid-bloom look.
exemplars.notes: ORIGINAL render (Replicate black-forest-labs/flux-2-pro, ~$0.06). Subject deliberately distinct from any analyzed source template. Illustrates the family aesthetic target (palette/composition/lighting); does NOT demonstrate runtime motion or in-engine execution.
